No `version` statement in any do-file. Stata's behaviour depends on the version, so a rerun must choose one and log it.
R code loads LandUseR, grateful, libpath, project, usethis, version, which code/LandUseR/renv.lock does not pin.

Code downloads https://www.statistiques.developpement-durable.gouv.fr/sites/default/files/2018-12/Q_tcm_menage_0.csv at run time. The content may have changed since publication; a receipt must record its SHA-256 (link not checked).

Code downloads https://www.statistiques.developpement-durable.gouv.fr/sites/default/files/2019-01/Q_tcm_individu.csv at run time. The content may have changed since publication; a receipt must record its SHA-256 (link not checked).

Code downloads https://www.statistiques.developpement-durable.gouv.fr/sites/default/files/2019-01/Q_ind_lieu_teg.csv at run time. The content may have changed since publication; a receipt must record its SHA-256 (link not checked).
5 code lines use absolute paths from the authors' machines. A rerun must edit them, and each edit is a logged deviation.
The package refers to GPUs or CUDA. A CPU rerun may be slower or numerically different and must say so.
Requires Stata; the desk says it has it.
The package ships a container definition. A rerun can build it, but image tags and base images must be pinned by digest to be reproducible.

Files the code both writes and reads are already in the package: data-moments.csv, population.csv. A run may read these instead of recomputing them. A receipt must say whether it replayed them or recomputed them, and a matching output hash alone does not show recomputation.
Code reads system files (/etc/redhat-release), usually to detect the operating system. Not package inputs; a rerun on another OS may take a different branch.
1 file reads use paths built at run time (macros, globs, variables), so triage could not check that those inputs exist.
